name: Athmanatheswarar Temple, Tiruvalampozhil
deity: Shiva as Athmanatheswarar, with the goddess Vadivudai Nayaki
period: Ancient Shaiva shrine of the Kaveri delta, sung in the Tevaram (7th century)
summary: At Tiruvalampozhil near Kumbakonam, Shiva is worshipped as Athmanatheswarar, lord of the soul, in a Kaveri-delta shrine sung by Appar, where the eight Vasus are said to have worshipped to shorten their earthly birth.

sections.history: Tiruvalampozhil is an old Shaiva village in the Kaveri delta near Kumbakonam, and its temple is a Paadal Petra Sthalam praised by the saint Appar in the Tevaram, where the place is called Tiruvalampozhil. The Lord is worshipped as Athmanatheswarar, the lord of the soul, and the goddess as Vadivudai Nayaki. Inscriptions found at the temple support the literary references to the site, and the shrine, like its neighbours in the delta, was maintained and enlarged in stone by the Cholas and later Tamil patrons. It stands close to the Paadal Petra temple of Pushpavananathar at Tiruppoonthuruthi.
sections.architecture: The temple is built in the Dravidian manner of the delta, with a gopuram entrance, a pillared hall and a walled courtyard around the sanctum. The sanctum enshrines the Shiva linga of Athmanatheswarar, with the goddess Vadivudai Nayaki in her own shrine, and the usual parivara deities of a Shiva temple around the prakara. The modest scale and old stonework give it the feel of a classic delta village temple rather than a grand complex.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that the eight Vasus, the celestial beings, once stole the divine cow Kamadhenu and were cursed by a sage to be born on earth as men. Seeking to shorten their time in human birth, they are said to have come to this place and worshipped Shiva, who granted them release; from this the temple is honoured as a place where the soul finds its lord, fitting the name Athmanatheswarar.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri, the monthly Pradosham, and the Tamil month festivals are observed, along with the car festival that draws the surrounding villages. As a delta temple it keeps the Shaiva calendar of the Kaveri country. Festival dates follow the Tamil calendar, so confirm them locally.
sections.experience: Tiruvalampozhil offers the quiet of an old delta sanctuary away from the crowds, and is easily visited together with the nearby Paadal Petra temples of Tiruppoonthuruthi and the Thiruvaiyaru group. Devotees come to worship Athmanatheswarar and Vadivudai Nayaki, and to recall the legend of the Vasus who found release here.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvalampozhil lies near Tiruppoonthuruthi, a short distance from Kumbakonam and Thiruvaiyaru in Thanjavur district. Kumbakonam and Thanjavur are the nearest railheads; Tiruchirappalli airport is about 60 km away. Local buses and autos reach the village.
